title: Customer-visible approval UX and automated rollback triggers - PRD (draft)
body:
Status: DRAFT - working notes for PD. Owner: Claire Nguyen. Purpose: propose a lightweight, customer-visible approval UX and the set of automated rollback triggers we will ship for Private deployments. This doc focuses on operator/customer interactions, audit-log footprint, and concrete rollback conditions for safe, verifiable changes.

Background and motivation:
- Customers deploying customer-managed networking frequently want transparency into who approved network changes and the rationale.
- Our current approval system captures dev ops-level metadata but isn't surfaced to the customer in a concise, searchable way.
- Additionally, customers and ops teams want automated rollback on unsafe changes (misconfig, accidental wide open rules, service regressions). We need a deterministic set of triggers and a small audit payload for each change so both sides can validate and reproduce events.

Goals (explicit):
1) Provide a customer-facing approval card that summarizes the change, the approver identity, justification, and risk classification.
2) Emit a compact audit record per approval/change that is sufficient for forensics and replay without leaking secrets.
3) Define a small set of automated rollback triggers that are deterministic, testable, and configurable per-customer SLO.
4) Keep operator burden low: allow safe manual overrides with attestation logs.

Out of scope for MVP:
- Full policy-as-code authoring UI (we surface diffs only).
- Cross-customer analytics and ML-driven risk scoring (future).

MVP feature surface:
- Approval card (customer-visible):
  - Title: short, one-line summary of change (e.g., "Edge egress rule: allow Google IP range")
  - Who: approver name + role (e.g., "Marco Ruiz - Platform Ops")
  - Why: freeform short justification (max 280 chars)
  - Risk: enum {LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH} with short rationale tag (e.g., "HIGH - wide-open 0.0.0.0/0")
  - Time window: requested effective time + rollback window (default 15m / opt: 1h / 24h)
  - Audit link: one-click to download the compact proof bundle (see below)
  - Action buttons (customer-facing, if customer delegated approval): Approve | Reject | Require changes

- Compact audit record (per change) fields (MVP):
  - event_id: stable UUID string
  - timestamp_utc: ISO8601 string
  - actor: approver name + id (internal id only; customer sees name/role)
  - change_summary: single-line plain text
  - diff_hash: short SHA256 of the serialized diff (to enable tamper detection)
  - risk_class: enum string
  - effective_window: start/end timestamps
  - rollback_policy_id: reference to active rollback policy
  - attestation_chain: list of signer ids (min 1) - stored as signer ids, not keys
  - non-sensitive metadata tags: environment, region, policy_version
  - retention_tier: e.g., "90d-standard"
Note: The above will be serialized as a compact JSONL line in the audit stream. We intentionally omit secrets, full configs, and raw keys.

- Proof bundle download (for forensics): small gzipped bundle containing:
  - human-readable diff (text)
  - audit record JSON (see fields above)
  - operator comments (if any)
  - pointer to raw encrypted artifact (S3/GCS id) for authorized retrieval
This bundle is downloadable by authorized customer admins and our support with ACL checks.

Automated rollback triggers (MVP set):
- Trigger A: Error spike
  - Condition: service 5xx rate increases by +300% vs baseline within 5 minutes and absolute 5xx > 0.5% of requests
  - Action: immediate soft-rollback to previous active configuration; open an incident; notify approvers
- Trigger B: Latency SLO breach
  - Condition: p95 latency increases beyond configured SLO by >30% for 10 minutes
  - Action: rollback, mark change as suspect, create audit entry with reason code "latency-slo"
- Trigger C: Explict security flag (signature mismatch / diff_hash mismatch)
  - Condition: upon replay, the diff_hash for the applied change doesn't match the audit record (possible tampering or truncated deployment)
  - Action: automatic disable of the application of that change, escalate to security, emit forensic proof bundle generation
- Trigger D: Customer cancel within grace window
  - Condition: customer clicks "revoke" from approval card within effective rollback window
  - Action: immediate rollback, mark change as customer-revoked, log justification text

Rollback behaviour notes:
- Rollbacks are "soft" by default: revert the high-level routing/config delta rather than restore full snapshot of infra (minimize blast radius). For risky changes we may require a controlled rollback that triggers a canary first.
- Rollback attempts should include the change event_id and the rollback reason code and be persisted in the audit stream.
- Rollback must be idempotent and safe to call multiple times; implement a short-lived lock per-event_id to avoid repeated concurrent rollbacks.

UX specifics and copy (draft):
- Approval card header: "Pending change: <summary>"
- Risk badge: color-coded (green/orange/red) with tooltip: "Risk assigned by operator at approval time. Can be recalculated by audit flows."
- CTA text: Approve -> "Authorize change and start effective window"; Reject -> "Block change"; Require changes -> "Request clarifying change from operator"
- Revoke flow (customer): visible on card for the rollback window with warning text: "Revoking will attempt to revert the change. This may not be instantaneous and could affect in-flight sessions."

Security & access model:
- Only customer admins with role 'network-admin' may Approve/Reject/Revok e changes in customer-visible UI. Approvals done by our operators are displayed but customers can require their own re-approval before effect.
- Audit record storage: append-only, tamper-evidence via diff_hash and signed signer ids. Retention tiers per-customer policy.

Operational playbook (brief):
- If automated rollback fires, system creates incident with severity mapping, pings oncall and approvers.
- Manual override allowed via signed attestation: operator must provide justification that is persisted in audit bundle. Manual override requires 2-person attestations for HIGH risk changes.

Open questions / decisions to resolve:
1) How to compute baseline for error/latency triggers for new customers? Rolling baseline vs static pre-change window? (preference: rolling window anchored to 7 days, fallback to 24h if insufficient data)
2) Should diff_hash be calculated over canonicalized config (YAML sorting) or raw patch? (preference: canonicalized)
3) Default rollback window length (15m) — ask CS for common patterns.
4) Should customers be able to define custom triggers? MVP: no; future: yes via policy templates.

Implementation notes and tech debt:
- Audit pipeline: create a lightweight JSONL stream separate from raw telemetry; this stream will be forwarded to customer S3/GCS if configured and to internal long-term cold store.
- Approval card UI: small React component in Console; reuse existing change-detail component.
- Rollback executor: idempotent: lookup last-good-state by event lineage; if lineage not available, fallback to inverse of diff (best effort) and open ticket.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Within 60 days of launch, 80% of customer-initiated private network changes have an approval card attached and accessible in the Console.
- Automated rollback prevents at least 50% of changes leading to sustained SLO breaches in the first 30m post-change (measured on pilot customers).
- Mean time to rollback action initiation < 3 minutes for Trigger A/B in pilot.

Milestones (high-level):
- Week 0-3: finalize audit record schema, attach diff_hash generator, design UI copy
- Week 4-8: build approval card UI + API + audit JSONL stream
- Week 9-12: implement rollback executor and basic triggers (A,B,D) + internal testing
- Week 13-16: pilot with 2 customers + iterate on trigger thresholds

Links and references: see linked_artifacts for tickets. Slack thread: #private-deploy-safety (search: "approval card rollback")

Next steps (immediate):
- Get CS input on default rollback window (action: ping Anika)
- SRE to confirm baseline computation approach (action: tag SRE Oncall)
- Design to produce first UI mockup for approval card by 2026-02-28

Notes to self: keep audit record minimal and non-sensitive. Resist temptation to include raw ACLs in UX; provide proof bundle for authorized retrieval.
summary: Draft PRD for a customer-visible approval card and deterministic automated rollback triggers tailored to Private deployments. Focus on compact audit records, simple UX, and safe default rollback behaviour.
